record.paper_title: Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can MARL agents learn human-intelligible and interpretable communication protocols that communicate causal relationships between agents, and would such causal communication improve learning efficiency in decentralized tasks?

evidence.quote: Such communication methods are often less natural than real-world emergent behaviour displayed by human communication, and there is room for research for emergent human intelligible and interpretable communication.

One can imagine that communicating causal relationships could greatly boost learning efﬁciency in decentralised tasks, similar to how Vanneste et al. (2020) improve credit assignment using counterfactual knowledge. This is potentially a fruitful direction for multi-agent, causal research.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a decentralized cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning setting modeled as a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process (Dec-POMDP) defined by a tuple (N, S, {A_i}, {O_i}, P, R, γ), where N is a finite set of agents, S a state space, A_i and O_i the action and observation spaces of agent i, P a transition kernel, R a shared reward function, and γ ∈ (0,1) a discount factor. Augment the model with a communication channel: at each time step every agent i emits a message m_i drawn from a finite alphabet M, observed by the other agents before they choose their actions. Each agent is also equipped with a structural causal model (SCM) over a set of variables describing its local environment and the joint state-action history, which induces interventional and counterfactual distributions in the sense of Pearl.

Formulate and resolve the following two questions:

(1) Existence of interpretable causal protocols. Does there exist a learning algorithm and a communication policy {π^c_i : history → Δ(M)} such that, with high probability over training, the emergent messages m_i are human-intelligible and interpretable in the following precise sense: there is a (learned) decoding function D : M → C, where C is a class of statements about causal relationships (interventional or counterfactual claims drawn from the agents' SCMs) of bounded description length, such that D(m_i) is, with high probability, a true statement about the underlying SCM at the time m_i is sent?

(2) Efficiency benefit of causal communication. Compare the sample complexity (number of environment interactions needed to reach an ε-optimal joint policy) of (a) decentralized MARL without communication, (b) decentralized MARL with arbitrary learned communication, and (c) decentralized MARL restricted to communication of true causal statements as in (1). Prove or disprove that there exists a non-trivial family of Dec-POMDPs on which option (c) has strictly lower sample complexity than (a) and (b), quantifying the gap.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction at the intersection of causal inference and multi-agent reinforcement learning. A web check finds related work on emergent communication and on counterfactual credit assignment in MARL, but no published result establishes either the existence of provably interpretable causal communication protocols or a formal sample-complexity separation in favour of causal communication. The problem appears to remain open as a formal mathematical question.

status_evidence.title: Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists interpretable causal communication and its impact on learning efficiency as an open research direction.
status_evidence.claim: The question is identified as an open direction in the causal MARL literature.
